childNodes.textContent: Remix 19 — Shapeshifter, cyan · Build once. Sell to many.

One page, three themes (so they can't drift apart):
       light (default)  remix 13 — a plain header, no shader anywhere
       ?theme=shader    remix 14 — a live Warp shader behind the whole page,
                        the wordmark intro, glass surfaces (14-dark-shader/
                        redirects here with ?theme=shader).
       ?theme=shape     remix 17 — remix 04's shapeshifter house style: paper,
                        black rules, hard shadows, acid accent, wide uppercase
                        type (17-shapeshifter/ redirects here with
                        ?theme=shape&layout=mvp).
       &ss=brand        remix 18 — the shapeshifter theme in EAI's colours,
                        with the Paper Warp shaders behind the big slabs
                        (18-shapeshifter-brand/ redirects here).
       &ss=cyan         remix 19 — remix 17 with EAI cyan (#8EDFF9) in place
                        of the acid green (19-shapeshifter-cyan/).
       ?theme=cfg       remix 20 — the Configurator brand (Brand Book v3), on white
       ?theme=refined   remix 21 — remix 01's Refined style
       Remix 22 is remix 19 with ?layout=mvp-multi (the multiplier wall).
       Remix 23 is remix 19 with ?layout=mvp2 (V2 user testing: the retest page).
       ?theme=brand     remix 24 — the V2 page in brand book v4 (bright grey,
                        navy marks, cyan underline), as in socials/BRAND.md
       Remix 25 is remix 24 with ?layout=mvp3 (V3: the V2 page plus app settings
                        you can click through and "Build in your CLI. Manage in
                        EAI."). mvp3 runs as mvp2 with data-v="3" on <html>, so
                        23 and 24 don't change.
       Remix 26 is remix 25 with &site=1: this page as the home page of the
                        V3 site (../26-site/), with the site's menu and footer
                        in place of the section links.
       &lp=<key>        27 — remix 25 as a landing page for one of brand book
                        v5's five taglines (landing.js; ../27-taglines/).

attributes.aria-label: Enterprise AI, back to the top

childNodes.textContent:
Every top-level section below carries data-section (its key in
       ?order= / ?hide=) and data-label (its name in the Arrange tool). None
       depends on its position: arrange.js can put any of them first. The
       closing CTA and the footer stay put.
============ Chat: what do you want to build? ============
============ The builder demo (always on the page; auto-plays in view) ============

============ The multiplier (from remix 03): one build, sold again and again.
       Only shown by layouts that ask for it (?layout=mvp-multi, remix 22). ============
============ Sugar hit 2: on their phone (12's section, following the build) ============
============ Gofer: we don't just build the process, we improve it ============
============ Control: EAI Curate + Workflows (V2 user testing only) ============
============ Build in your CLI, manage in EAI (V3, manage.js) ============

============ Who it's for (remix 29, the lean site) ============
       Hidden unless ?site=1&ia=2, when ../26-site/site.js shows it. The
       lean site has no "who we help" or examples pages: this is where
       they went. No data-section, so the Arrange tool and every other
       remix never see it. The copy is those pages' own. "See use cases"
       opens the AI features' use-case list (use-cases.js).
Three kinds of team build on Enterprise AI. Each starts with one workflow.
Give client one a tailored result, keep an authorised delivery foundation, then adapt it for client two while confidential material stays contained.
turn an authorised delivery method into a reusable foundation, with each client’s data kept separate.
Help teams find missing evidence, focus review effort and take the next authorised action from one case flow.
move supplier evidence from intake to a review-ready case, with final approval kept with a named reviewer.
Combine reusable workflow capability with your product context, customer relationships and market expertise.
add a controlled workflow to a customer journey, with integration, product and support responsibilities agreed before release.
These are illustrative workflows, not customer results.
Named stories are published once their evidence, wording and customer permission are approved.

============ Pricing (remix 26, and the tagline pages) ============
       Hidden unless ?site=1, when ../26-site/site.js shows it, or ?lp=, when
       landing.js shows it with a sign-up button on each plan; no
       data-section, so the Arrange tool and 23, 24 and 25 never see it.
       The four plans from the signed-in workspace (PLANS in
       workspace-ai-demo/assets/admin-app-tier.js), as on
       ../26-site/pricing.html: keep the three in step.
Pick a plan and how many credits you need each month.

childNodes.textContent: Gofer: distil it to four steps
We don’t just build the process. We make it better.
Tell Gofer how the work gets done today, however messy. It hands back the same job in four steps, ready to build.
Turns any process into four steps
Here’s how we get a campaign email out for Nike today:
Marketing emails the brief to the agency
Brief rewritten into a Word template
Designer hunts for the brand guide and shots
Asks on Teams for the latest product shots
Draft pasted into the tracking sheet
Changes go back and forth, three rounds
Copy keyed into the email platform
That’s 12 steps across 6 tools, and 4 of them are re-typing or chasing. Here’s the same job in four:
The brief is one form, so nobody re-types it.
AI drafts the copy in Nike’s voice.
Brand and Legal approve together, in one step.
Same four steps, ready for the builder.
Paste how the work gets done today…

childNodes.textContent: Switch on AI. Watch the app get smarter.
Each one is a switch, not a project. Here’s what each does inside the app, for every client this build serves.
Upload the handbook and the assistant answers from it, with the page it found each answer on. Every client’s copy answers from their own documents.
It lists every document a step needs, ticks off what’s in and flags what’s missing, so nobody submits half a file.
Each upload is read against your rules (name matches, not expired, signed) and the ones that fail are flagged before a person looks.
It drafts the contract from answers already in the app, ready to sign and send for approval.
Answers from the staff handbook, with sources.
Fortnightly, on Thursdays. Your first is 24 Oct.

Paste how the work gets done today…
Here’s how we get a campaign email out for Nike today:
Marketing emails the brief to the agency
Brief rewritten into a Word template
Designer hunts for the brand guide and shots
Asks on Teams for the latest product shots
Draft pasted into the tracking sheet
Changes go back and forth, three rounds
Copy keyed into the email platform
That’s 12 steps across 6 tools, and 4 of them are re-typing or chasing. Here’s the same job in four:
Fortnightly, on Thursdays. Your first is 24 Oct.

The brief is one form, so nobody re-types it.
AI drafts the copy in Nike’s voice.
Brand and Legal approve together, in one step.
